value.body: Central ministries, banks and public-sector companies employ staff to translate documents between Hindi and English and to implement the Official Language (Rajbhasha) policy. Central posts such as Junior Hindi Translator and Junior Translation Officer are filled through an SSC exam; banks recruit Rajbhasha Adhikari (official-language officers) through specialist-officer recruitment.

items.label: Bank route
items.note: Specialist officer posts, for example through IBPS SO

items.label: Usual qualification
items.note: With the other language studied at degree level; some posts also ask for a translation diploma or experience

items.label: Age limit for SSC translator posts
items.source: SSC Combined Hindi Translators Exam notice (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Finish a B.A. with Hindi and/or English, then a Master's in one of them. Apply when SSC or the bank recruitment bodies notify posts; the exams test translation, both languages and general knowledge of the subject.

value.title: At a glance
items: A B.A. alone usually does not meet the qualification; the Master's is the gate.
Vacancies are notified once a year or less and vary widely between cycles.
State governments and PSUs also hire for official-language work through their own notices.

value.title: Vacancies in the SSC Combined Hindi Translators Examination
value.note: SSC vacancy counts are tentative and often revised (2025 rose from 437 to 552; 2026 was revised from 84 to 303 regular posts). Bank Rajbhasha Adhikari posts are not included.
value.source: SSC Combined Hindi Translators Examination notices (as reported)
